deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about -1% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 250% last year; 105%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 87% (3 years ago -10%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $87 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 61% (3 years ago -13%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $134.0B — about 1.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $13.0B, up from $169M a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 105%/yr over 3 years and 37%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 75% vs a 5-year range of -41–75% (median 24%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $1.3B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($650M buybacks + $610M dividends) = 0.2% of the company's market value. Share count up 1.8% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $204.99, up 20% in 90 days (down 1% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $176.18, up 13% in 90 days; 1 analyst raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers

deeper.title: Where sales come from

deeper.title: Insider trading

summary.thesis: Micron is an A-grade business trading at 8.1 times trailing earnings, but the price is in a downtrend, and the open question is whether its record 74.59% operating margin can last.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, and buy only near the 471.0 support or after the 2026-12-17 report shows the margin holding. Swing: no trade.
summary.act_at: Buy at 471.0; back to hold on a close above 659.6; trim above 833.11

note.happening: MU fell 4.53% to 601.25, after a drop to 629.79 the day before. It now trades below its 20-day (742.8), 200-day (776.3) and 50-day (895.41) averages, and the trend reads as down. There is no new news, and the next earnings report is on 2026-12-17.
note.business: Nothing in today's data changes the business. The latest filed numbers (quarter ended 2026-09-03) are still exceptional: trailing revenue of 133.2B against 37.4B a year earlier, free cash flow of 59.0B against 1.7B, and 40.6B in net cash. The thing at risk is margin, not survival. The operating margin is 74.59%, up from 26.14%, and the filings flag that it sits at the top of its 5-year range (-41% to 75%), where peaks 'usually fade'. Memory chip prices tend to move in cycles (general knowledge), so the earnings power is real today but may not be permanent. What is not at risk: the balance sheet. Cash of 38.4B dwarfs debt of 2.8B, and dilution is low at 1.78% a year. The past two days' fall is a sentiment and trend story: the technical and macro inputs are negative, while the fundamental read stays positive.

worth.text: The usual cash-flow model is switched off, because free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year and that jump can't be projected forward. So two other angles are used. First, against its own history, the price-to-sales ratio (price divided by yearly revenue per share) puts fair value between 322.32 and 833.11, with a middle of 490.66. Second, a reverse view: the current price implies free cash flow shrinking 4.6% a year from here. If cash flow merely holds flat, the model gives 720.9. Even if the operating margin halves to 37%, the model gives 800.71, but that figure assumes 20% starting growth, which is generous. Against peers, MU looks cheap: price-to-sales of 5.1 against a peer median of 7.6, and 0.28 on a growth-adjusted basis. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption: whether today's 59.0B of free cash flow is a new base or a cyclical peak. Fair-value range: 490.66 to 720.9.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near 59.0B instead of shrinking as the 74.59% operating margin fades from the top of its 5-year range.

bull: The price implies free cash flow shrinking 4.6% a year, while flat cash flow would be worth 720.9 per share.
At 8.1 times trailing earnings and 5.1 times sales, against a peer median of 7.6, the stock is cheap for an A-grade business (quality score 88).
40.6B of net cash and 59.0B of trailing free cash flow give a large cushion if the cycle turns.
bear: The 74.59% operating margin, up from 26.14%, sits at the top of a 5-year range that reached as low as -41%, and the filings note that such peaks usually fade.
The price is in a downtrend below a falling 50-day average of 895.41, and the nearest strong support zone (435.76–471.0) sits well below the price.
Options price a 19.1% move by the 2026-12-18 expiry, and put open interest is 1.98 times call open interest, which shows traders paying for protection.

levels.what: Top of the 435.76–471.0 support zone (a price floor), which has held 5 times and sits near the 490.66 own-history middle. Buy here.
Top of the 642.41–659.6 resistance zone (a ceiling) that the price lost. A close above it moves the call back to hold.

longterm.why: At 601.25 the price sits inside the 490.66–720.9 fair-value range, so it is not cheap enough to give a margin of safety before the margin question is answered. The downtrend gives no reason to buy early.

swing.why: The trend is down, and resistance starts at 642.41, close above the price, so there is little upside before it. The nearest support is 471.0, far below, so a sensible stop would sit too far away to justify the trade.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-17 report lands one day before the 2026-12-18 options expiry, which prices a 19.1% move. There is no new long-term position until that report shows whether the operating margin holds, unless the price reaches 471.0 first.

change_mind: A close above 659.6, back through the lost resistance zone, would move the long-term call from wait to hold.
If the 2026-12-17 report shows the operating margin holding near 74.59% with free cash flow near 59.0B, that supports the 720.9 flat-growth value, and the call would move to buy below that level.
A close below 435.76, the bottom of the main support zone, would push the buy level down to the 351.92–369.12 zone.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait. The 4.53% drop to 601.25 kept the price below the 642.41–659.6 zone that would restore a hold, and it is still well above the 471.0 buy level.
